pr_title: xdg-decoration: let floating clients set borders
pr_body:
The xdg-decoration protocol allows clients to request whether they want
to use server side decorations or client side decorations. Currently,
sway ignores this and always enforces whatever the server is currently
set to. Although tiled clients cannot be allowed to set borders, there
is no harm in listening requests from floating clients. First,
handle_map needs to check if the client has requested client side
decorations and flip the csd bool to true if it has. Secondly,
xdg_decoration_handle_request_mode needs to also check if a client
requests a different mode and update the container if applicable.
Sidenote: also fixed an unrelated style error.

I didn't check, but I think this would fix #6414 assuming this is how SDL requests a borderless window.
pr_comments: Testing with the `toplevel-decoration` example in wlroots, it seems like this doesn't behave correctly in tiled mode. `toplevel-decoration client` gets client-side decorations in tiled mode it seems, but Sway should force server-side decorations in this case.
Oops, the old border needs to be saved in the floating toggle. It should work now.

With that comment fixed, it doesn't seem like this patch is enough to make floating views use CSD if they were initially tiled. Maybe something wrong with the CSD logic inside `container_set_floating`?
I changed the floating check to an if/else based on if the view has a container. It seems to work.

Actually, is the `wants_floating` check even needed? It seems like `view_update_csd_from_client` handles it fine and `wlr_xdg_toplevel_decoration_v1_set_mode` doesn't cause any ill effects if the window is tiled.

Okay, I think I got it now. `view_update_csd_from_client` and such always needs to be called as long as there is a container but `wants_floating` needs to be checked so sway sends the correct mode on the configure event. Additionally, toggling floating needs to also send configure events if the container is using csd.

This seems to behave a lot better, nice! I'm getting segfaults with some clients, because not all clients support the xdg-decoration protocol. e.g.

issue_context.title: SDL_WINDOW_BORDERLESS doesn't work on wayland sway, but works on xwayland sway
issue_context.body:
**Sway Version:** 1.6.1
**Debug Log:** https://gist.github.com/1ace/59d502f9c82ba2f2123f34752a04c48e#file-sway-log
**Configuration File:** https://gist.github.com/1ace/59d502f9c82ba2f2123f34752a04c48e#file-sway-config
**Description:**

As the title says, SDL's `SDL_WINDOW_BORDERLESS` only works when talking to sway through xwayland, but not when talking directly wayland to sway.

Expected behaviour: the window decorations are not shown
Actual behaviour on wayland sway: the window decorations are shown regardless of the flag (incorrect)
Actual behaviour on xwayland sway: the window decorations are not shown (correct)

Everything needed to reproduce the issue is in this gist: https://gist.github.com/1ace/59d502f9c82ba2f2123f34752a04c48e
In `run.sh`, replace `SDL_VIDEODRIVER=wayland` with `SDL_VIDEODRIVER=x11` to reproduce the xwayland behaviour.
comments:
Do you have a `WAYLAND_DEBUG=1` log?

Might be xdg-decoration related.
Ah, sorry, I forgot to mention: can you collect a `WAYLAND_DEBUG=1` log of the client? That is, set it then run the client, redirecting its output to a file?

sorry, I should've known that :sweat_smile:
app's wayland log: https://gist.github.com/1ace/870f5a58f39687654c62479802295d30

Looking at SDL's source, it seems like that if SDL_WINDOW_BORDERLESS is specified, it tells the compositor to use server-side decorations, and otherwise to use client-side decorations? I don't see any code that would actually result in there not being any borders at all.
Edit: That is, unless SDL has been compiled with libdecor. At the very least, Arch doesn't provide libdecor except via the AUR, so SDL2 on Arch won't go through that code path.

It's the other way around: with `BORDERLESS` it requests CSD, otherwise SSD ([`src/video/wayland/SDL_waylandwindow.c:991`](https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL/blob/d4e1b4974ac8711cc89bd187c9f412f84771372b/src/video/wayland/SDL_waylandwindow.c#L991)) and I haven't looked at that code but presumably the CSD is "nothing" which why it ends up borderless.

And yeah, [`libdecor`](https://gitlab.gnome.org/jadahl/libdecor) is not very popular yet, but hopefully it will catch on :)
I know that at least electron is going to be relying on it in the next release to work around Gnome's refusal to support SSD.

In any case, I'm not using the `libdecor` code path, so you can ignore that for this issue :slightly_smiling_face:
Ah, sorry, I had a brainfart and didn't realize `bordered = !borderless`

review_comments: I think we're missing `transaction_commit_dirty` right after
Hm, it seems like this lets the client do whatever it wants, even if tiled?

I'm not sure about this part. It seems like it is too early in the process to check for floating? At least if I do `view->impl->wants_floating && view->impl->wants_floating(view)`, that always returns false if the client is just started up (hacked an app-id into toplevel-decoration to easily make the window start up as floating).
At map-time, the view should always have a container, so `container_is_floating` could be used.
Ah. But only after the `view_map` call. Hmm.
Actually, `view_update_csd_from_client` already checks for `container_is_floating`. So nvm, we should be all good.
Oh oops, I missed the other comments on this. I'll put the logic back in `xdg_shell.c`.
